text:
carol: FYI CI mkdocs build just failed on latest docs deploy, getting a bunch of 404s for links that worked locally :thinking_face:
carol: error logs point to slug mismatch between `src/Guides/QuickStart.md` and generated anchor `/guides/quick-start` vs `/Guides/QuickStart` on Windows runners
miguel: hmm that screams case-sensitive filesystem vs case-insensitive. Which plugin are we using to slugify headings?
carol: default mkdocs slugify via python-markdown, but I also see warnings about image alt text: `WARNING - Documentation link 'assets/img/robot.PNG' not found` even though file exists with different case
sam: I ran into this before — our published site canonicalizes paths to lowercase during build because use_directory_urls is true and the plugin set lower_case_urls: true in a prior PR. That was intended for SEO but broke mixed-case filenames.
anya: quick remediation: add a pre-commit check to normalize filenames to kebab-case and enforce lowercase for URLs. I can draft a small script.
miguel: yes please. Also worth toggling the slugify variant to github-slugger to match docusaurus-style anchors — less surprise for contributors.
carol: small reproduction steps: (in CI)
```
mkdocs build -d site
# see warnings: WARN - 404 for /guides/QuickStart and /assets/img/robot.PNG
```
carol: PR  #3421 attempts to fix by renaming files to lowercase and updating links, but it touches ~30 files so I'd like a safer patch first.
sam: can we instead add a mkdocs plugin config to preserve case or normalize when generating slugs? Example in mkdocs.yml:
```
plugins:
  - search
  - slugify: { separator: "-", lowercase: true }
```
sam: but note lowercase:true would still make anchors lowercase which might mismatch older anchors in other sites — messy.
anya: here's a tiny pre-merge script I tested locally: `find docs -type f \( -iname "*.md" -o -iname "*.png" \) | while read f; do lc=$(echo "$f" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'); if [ "$f" != "$lc" ]; then mv "$f" "$lc"; git add "$lc"; fi; done` — it normalizes files and stages them.
carol: that would be fine as an opt-in check for doc contributors, run in CI job `docs-normalize`. Can we instead run a linkcheck step to fail builds with mixed-case mismatches before deploy?
miguel: yes add `mkdocs build --strict` to CI and run linkcheck plugin. Also we should update CONTRIBUTING.md to recommend lowercase filenames for assets.
carol: I've pushed a small PR #3429 that does three things: adds `docs-normalize` CI step, updates mkdocs.yml to use `slugify` plugin explicitly, and adds a CONTRIBUTING note. It leaves content filenames alone for now (safer).
anya: reviewing now. Found one risky change: slugify plugin options differ between versions; older version uses `slugify: true` rather than object. CI on the older runner fails the YAML parse.
sam: ugh. Which runner versions do we have? actions/ubuntu-20.04 vs 22.04?
carol: CI matrix includes ubuntu-20.04 image with mkdocs 1.2.2; our slugify plugin was updated in mkdocs 1.3. The fix: pin plugin version in `requirements-docs.txt` and install before build.
miguel: good catch. Please add `pip install -r docs/requirements-docs.txt` step in CI and pin `mkdocs-slugify==0.3.1` (example).
carol: updated PR #3429 with that change. Running CI... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
docs-bot: CI run started for PR #3429 (mkdocs: slugify + normalize job)
carol: CI passed on 22.04 but 20.04 still erroring because of an old pip cache on the runner — retrying build on that matrix.
docs-bot: Re-run requested by carol — job queued
miguel: once CI is green, let's do a small follow-up PR to lowercase only asset filenames that actually break builds, rather than sweeping renames. That reduces churn in history.
anya: agreed. I'll prepare a script to diff broken link list from linkcheck output and only rename those files automatically; draft commit will be reviewed.
carol: CI green on all matrix entries, linkcheck clean. PR #3429 ready for review.
sam: LGTM from me. Quick manual spot-check on dev site shows anchors now consistent and images rendering. :thumbsup:
carol: merging to main and kicking a docs deploy now.
deploy-bot: Deploy started for commit 7a4b2c3 (docs) to production :rocket:
carol: monitoring live site for 5 minutes — will ping if any regressions.
deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: https://docs.redwood.ai (SHA 7a4b2c3)
carol: site looks good, closing this thread. Thanks everyone! :tada:
